findings: ETT.tex:1734-1743, proof-level. « Strong causality provides a relatively compact open neighbourhood U_p of p, causally convex in M and contained in a chart with model E_kappa » followed by « Lemma restriction_convexe turns properties 3 and 4 of the model into properties 3 and 4 of U_p ». Applying lem:restriction_convexe in the model needs phi(U_p) causally convex in the model, and U_p causally convex in M does not give it. Lean witness: Causal.MeasuresManifolds.cutDiamond_separates. M = E^{1,2} minus the point (0,0) (the open set puncture), the chart is the inclusion into E^{1,2} (a chart isomorphism, SFATransfer.chartIso_restrOpen_refl), and U_p is the open diamond I((-2,0),(2,0)) with its centre removed (cutDiamond). It is open, relatively compact, inside the chart and causally convex in M (cutDiamond_causallyConvexIn_puncture), and its image is not causally convex in E^{1,2}: (0,0) lies between (-1,0) and (1,0) (not_cutDiamond_causallyConvexIn_top). This checks AUDIT-1 note (8) of T-ett-measures-e0, which was left unchecked. The proposition is not affected. Repair (formalized): choose U' causally convex in the model first (the models are strongly causal) and put U_p = phi^{-1}(U'). U_p is then causally convex in M by strong causality of M and causal arc-connectedness (Causal.MeasuresManifolds.ChartIso.causallyConvexIn_source_inter_preimage), and the transfer through the chart needs no convexity (ChartIso.admissiblePastOn). Suggested wording: « Strong causality provides a neighbourhood V of p inside a chart phi with model E_kappa, causally convex in M; let U' be a relatively compact open neighbourhood of phi(p) inside phi(V), causally convex in E_kappa, and U_p = phi^{-1}(U'), which is causally convex in M. [...] Lemma restriction_convexe turns properties 3 and 4 of the model into properties 3 and 4 of U', hence, through phi, of U_p ».

The planner's [r] route (2026-11-21, the sharpened one), checked step by step. It is correct. (1) U = phi^{-1}(U') cap S is causally convex in M as claimed. The step x <=_S y (the causal curve from x to y stays in the diamond J(x, y), inside V, inside S) is Causal.MeasuresManifolds.le_of_causallyConvexIn_of_subset, the proof of le_iff_of_causallyConvexIn with V inside S, 6 lines. (2) Only DEC-7's StronglyCausal enters. Neither tarentin nor causal openness of M is used. U' is taken inside e.target cap e.symm^{-1}(V), a neighbourhood of phi(p) by continuity of phi^{-1}, so interior V is not needed. (3) The K-transport lemma is Causal.MeasuresManifolds.mem_Kminus_of_intertwine, then ChartIso.symm_mem_Kminus_iff. It needs only the continuity of the inverse at the points involved and the matching of <=. The sequences of M are handled by passing to a tail where v n lies in the image (max N N1). (4) Carried, finite and regular pass through the homeomorphism U ~ e(U) (OpenPartialHomeomorph.homeomorphOfImageSubsetSource, Measure.Regular.map) and admissiblePastOn_map_subtype_iff. That needs R1Space M, which the route did not mention; the paper's Hausdorff hypothesis carries it. (5) The family instances by cases on o reduce by rfl, and no second MeasurableSpace (Cone kappa) is declared. (6) Refinement: V can be taken inside e.source cap N for any neighbourhood N of p. This gives the local form at M (ModelMeasuresLocal C), so U_p can be found in every neighbourhood, and relatively compact when M is locally compact Hausdorff, as the paper has it. Every line reference of the block checked: SingularGeroch.lean:174, :188; MeasuresE0.lean:457, :484, :607, :713, :742, :827; MeasuresEAlpha.lean:615; ArcConnected.lean:356, :456, :464; Reachable.lean:98; MassADEC25.lean:358; E0Strong.lean:759; Massive.lean:209; GlobalHyperbolicity.lean:226.

Model side at the regular points: the paper's charts « with model E_kappa » (l.1735-1736) include the charts into E^{1,2} (= E_{2pi}) of the maximal a.e. atlas. There the measure is a finite measure with the null sets of lambda_3 on R x R^2, restricted to a causally convex open set (Causal.MeasuresManifolds.minkowski_modelMeasuresLocal, via MeasuresEAlpha.static_admissiblePastOn_restrict_of). Not a defect of the paper.

kb_proposals: Measures through a chart isomorphism: Causal.MeasuresManifolds.ChartIso.admissiblePastOn / admissibleFutureOn carry a measure admissible on e(U) back to U for every open U in the source; no causal convexity is needed, only R1Space M. Choose the model's set first: ChartIso.exists_admissiblePastOn (U = e^{-1}(U'), U' causally convex in the model, inside any neighbourhood, e(U) = U'). Assembled as ModelMeasuresLocal and isoChartsCover_modelMeasures(Local); at E_{>=0}-manifolds massA_modelMeasures(Local), at E_0-manifolds e0Manifold_modelMeasures(Local) (T-ett-measures-manifolds).

Pitfall: U causally convex in M does not make its chart image causally convex in the model. Witness: Causal.MeasuresManifolds.cutDiamond_separates (E^{1,2} minus a point, the cut diamond). Pick U' convex in the model, then prove U = e^{-1}(U') convex in M (ChartIso.causallyConvexIn_source_inter_preimage, via le_of_causallyConvexIn_of_subset: a convex V inside an open S gives <=_S from <=_M under causal arc-connectedness) (T-ett-measures-manifolds).

K^- through a bijection of open sets matching <=: Causal.MeasuresManifolds.mem_Kminus_of_intertwine (the inverse continuous on U'); through a chart isomorphism ChartIso.symm_mem_Kminus_iff, both directions from the one lemma with the roles swapped. K^-_U is read with sequences of M: pass to the tail of the sequence inside the open set (T-ett-measures-manifolds).
